question.text: An organic compound ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> ' with empirical formula <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math> gives sooty flame on burning. Its reaction with bromine solution in low polarity solvent results in high yield of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo> </mo><mo>.</mo><mo> </mo><mi>B</mi></math> is

solution.text: Compound A is phenol which gives sooty flame on burning. Its reaction with bromine solution in low polarity solvent results in high yield of 4-bromophenol.
